Weekly Support / Resistance — Multi-Region Backtest

Period 2023–2026 (≈3y) · 10 liquid tickers · 5 markets (US, HK, China A, Asia TYO/KS, EU) · strict no-lookahead · ~151 weeks evaluated per name

Winner: Weekly Pivot S1/R12nd: Prior-week low/highBearish: Volume POC & 50-day MA as hard walls

Method in one line

Every level is a zone: [L − w, L + w], width w = 0.5 × weekly ATR(14). A zone holds when a week touches it but its weekly close does not exit the far side. Respect = held ÷ touched. Levels are built from week-T data only and tested on week T+1 (no lookahead).

Respect rate — how often the zone HOLDS when actually touched

Rows colored: green ≥70%, amber 50–70%, red <50%. Higher is better.

Where quality lives — the "good quadrant"

Top-right = high touch and high respect = genuinely useful S/R. Weekly pivots (navy) sit top-right in every region; POC/MA (orange) hug the right edge with weak respect.

Hold-rate by region (when actually touched)

Support (green) beats resistance (red) in every market — the signature of net upward drift over the window. Monthly pivot S1 is the tallest, most reliable insurance level.

Worked examples

What worked (GOOD)

Weekly pivot S1/R1 — use everywhere. Respect 0.88–0.94 and touch 0.82–0.89 in all five markets. Fresh (built from the just-closed week), always near price, and self-adjusts to volatility drift. This is the default "next-week" level.
Prior-week low / high — strongest secondary level. Respect 0.70–0.80, touch 0.63–0.78; the classic institutional level, mildly weaker than pivots but nearly as reliable, and cheap.
Monthly pivot S1 — the insurance level. Respect 0.94–0.98 but low touch (~0.35). When price truly reaches a deep monthly support it almost never closes through it in the same week. Use as a second-line / invalidation reference, not a weekly trade trigger.
Support beats resistance everywhere (S1 0.90–0.94 vs R1 0.88–0.93; prior-week low 0.77–0.80 vs high 0.70–0.78). In an upward-drift world, demand-side levels survive better.

What failed (BAD)

12-month Volume POC as a hard wall — respect 0.21–0.56 with touch up to 0.95. POC is a center of gravity: price oscillates around it and routinely closes through it. Especially broken in trends (SAP resistance POC respect = 0.24).
50-day MA as resistance — respect 0.44–0.65. In uptrends price travels well above it, so treating it as "resistance" inverts reality; as support it is only middling.
Fix: recast both as mean / regime inputs for the ML-P(hold) and narrative layers — not as S/R boundaries.

Region-specific findings

  • China A-shares look deceptively powerful. Deep-level respect near 0.94 and POC/MA touch at 0.80–0.92. This is largely the ±10% daily price-limit illusion: the wall blocks single-week closes, so "respect" inflates; real breaks arrive as limit-gaps, not clean closes. Flag limit-moves before trusting A-share respect numbers.
  • Europe shows the trend artifact most. SAP's year-old volume POC / 50-day MAs collapse as resistance because the stock ground higher — any static level far from price is fake resistance in a trending name.
  • US is the cleanest, most textbook (monthly support 0.95–1.00, weekly pivot S1 0.93).
  • Hong Kong and Tokyo/Seoul Asia sit solidly mid-high across families; volume POC weakest here too (oscillation around the yearly average).

Bottom line & next steps

For a "next-week" S/R map, the cheap deterministic combo wins: weekly pivot S1/R1 as the primary bracket + prior-week low/high as confirmation + monthly pivot S1 as the deep insurance level. This measurably beats naive prior-period levels in the backtest.

What the numbers justify next: (1) add a China limit-move flag and re-run A-share names to separate true support from price-limit illusion; (2) feed the losers (POC, 50-day MA) into the ML P(hold) layer + options-IV range from the master plan as mean/regime context rather than boundaries — that is precisely where their information belongs.
